title: Roasted Red Pepper Soup
subtitle: Sweet roasted peppers blended with tomato and paprika
excerpt: Red peppers roasted until charred and sweet, then blended with tomato, stock, and smoked paprika into a vivid, deeply flavoured soup. Drizzle with a little crème fraîche to serve.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roasted red pepper soup draws on Spanish and Mediterranean cooking traditions where grilled peppers are a fundamental ingredient. The charred skins add a slight smokiness. The peppers must be fully blackened and steamed in a bag to allow the skins to peel cleanly. Smoked paprika reinforces the roasted flavour. This soup is naturally vegan unless finished with cream.

recipeTools.notes: For blending directly in the pot.

content.text: Roasting the peppers under a hot grill until fully blackened is the key step. Transfer them straight from the grill into a bowl covered with cling film or into a sealed bag: the steam loosens the skins in 15 minutes. The soup is very forgiving once the peppers are ready.

Place the pepper halves skin-side up on a baking sheet under a hot grill. Grill for 15 to 20 minutes, turning as needed, until the skins are heavily charred and blistered all over. Transfer to a bowl and cover tightly with cling film. Leave for 15 minutes to steam. Peel off and discard the skins.
While the peppers steam, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the peeled peppers and tinned tomatoes. Pour in the hot stock. Add the sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve in warmed bowls with a swirl of crème fraîche if desired and a drizzle of olive oil.
